extracted.intended_audience: Users of Isabelle/HOL (proof engineers, formal-methods practitioners, advanced students) who need reference for proof tools and code generation
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for Isabelle/Isar proof tools (quickcheck, nitpick, coercions, arithmetic provers, proof-search methods, algebraic solvers) and the code-generation framework (export_code and code_* attributes). Intended to guide correct use and configuration of these tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: value / values evaluation commands
rubrics_metrics.description:
value t evaluates and prints a term; optionally modes can be specified, which are appended to the current print mode; Evaluation is tried first using ML, falling back to normalization by evaluation if this fails. Alternatively a specific evaluator can be selected using square brackets; typical evaluators use the current set of code equations to normalize and include simp for fully symbolic evaluation using the simplifier, nbe for normalization by evaluation and code for code generation in SML.
values t enumerates a set comprehension by evaluation and prints its values up to the given number of solutions; optionally modes can be specified, which are appended to the current print mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use modes to control printing; choose evaluator (simp/nbe/code) per goal; evaluation prefers ML then nbe fallback. Use values to enumerate comprehension results up to a specified bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: quickcheck tests the current goal for counterexamples using a series of assignments for its free variables; by default the first subgoal is tested, another can be selected explicitly using an optional goal index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments can be chosen exhaustively up to a size, randomly, or by symbolic narrowing. By default quickcheck uses exhaustive testing. Use quickcheck to find counterexamples; configure behavior with quickcheck_params or inline options in square brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck tester option
rubrics_metrics.description: tester specifies which testing approach to apply. There are three testers, exhaustive, random, and narrowing. An unknown configuration option is treated as an argument to tester, making tester = optional. When multiple testers are given, these are applied in parallel. If no tester is specified, quickcheck uses the testers that are set active.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick tester according to problem: exhaustive for small finite search spaces, random for sampling, narrowing for symbolic exploration. Multiple testers can be combined/parallelized.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck size option
rubrics_metrics.description: size specifies the maximum size of the search space for assignment values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set size to limit exhaustive exploration; larger sizes increase search cost exponentially for many domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck genuine_only option
rubrics_metrics.description: genuine_only sets quickcheck only to return genuine counterexample, but not potentially spurious counterexamples due to underspecified functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable to filter out counterexamples that might be artefacts of underspecification; may mask useful diagnostic information if functions are intentionally underspecified.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck abort_potential option
rubrics_metrics.description: abort_potential sets quickcheck to abort once it found a potentially spurious counterexample and to not continue to search for a further genuine counterexample. For this option to be effective, the genuine_only option must be set to false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to stop early on potential problems; combine carefully with genuine_only depending on whether you want to continue search for genuine counterexamples.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck eval option
rubrics_metrics.description: eval takes a term or a list of terms and evaluates these terms under the variable assignment found by quickcheck. This option is currently only supported by the default (exhaustive) tester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use eval to inspect values computed at a counterexample assignment; supported only for exhaustive tester.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck iterations option
rubrics_metrics.description: iterations sets how many sets of assignments are generated for each particular size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase iterations to repeat searches per size (useful with random/narrowing strategies) to improve chance of finding counterexamples; increases runtime.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck no_assms option
rubrics_metrics.description: no_assms specifies whether assumptions in structured proofs should be ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set when you want to test goal ignoring local assumptions (e.g., to test the bare conclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck locale option
rubrics_metrics.description: locale specifies how to process conjectures in a locale context, i.e. they can be interpreted or expanded. The option is a whitespace-separated list of the two words interpret and expand. The list determines the order they are employed. The default setting is to first use interpretations and then test the expanded conjecture. The option is only provided as attribute declaration, but not as parameter to the command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose interpret/expand ordering to control how locale parameters are instantiated and conjectures expanded for testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck timeout option
rubrics_metrics.description: timeout sets the time limit in seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to bound testing time; prevents long-running exhaustive/random searches from blocking interactive sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck default_type option
rubrics_metrics.description: default_type sets the type(s) generally used to instantiate type variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide plausible default instantiations for polymorphic variables to guide testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck report option
rubrics_metrics.description: report if set quickcheck reports how many tests fulfilled the preconditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable to get statistics about precondition satisfaction across tests; useful for diagnosing why no counterexamples were found.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck use_subtype option
rubrics_metrics.description: use_subtype if set quickcheck automatically lifts conjectures to registered subtypes if possible, and tests the lifted conjecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable to consider subtype instances during testing, potentially revealing counterexamples relying on subtype structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck quiet and verbose options
rubrics_metrics.description:
quiet if set quickcheck does not output anything while testing.
verbose if set quickcheck informs about the current size and cardinality while testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quiet for non-interfering background checks; verbose for progress diagnostics during long tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck expect option
rubrics_metrics.description: expect can be used to check if the user’s expectation was met (no_expectation, no_counterexample, or counterexample).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use expect to assert testing outcome expectations as part of regression checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck_params and quickcheck_generator
rubrics_metrics.description:
quickcheck_params changes quickcheck configuration options persistently.
quickcheck_generator creates random and exhaustive value generators for a given type and operations. It generates values by using the operations as if they were constructors of that type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quickcheck_params for persistent setup. Use quickcheck_generator to obtain generators for custom types by providing constructor-like operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: quickcheck tester classes: exhaustive, random, narrowing
rubrics_metrics.description:
Using the following type classes, the testers generate values and convert them back into Isabelle terms for displaying counterexamples.
exhaustive: The parameters of the type classes exhaustive and full_exhaustive implement the testing. They take a testing function as a parameter, which takes a value of type 'a and optionally produces a counterexample, and a size parameter for the test values. In full_exhaustive, the testing function parameter additionally expects a lazy term reconstruction in the type Code_Evaluation.term of the tested value. The canonical implementation for exhaustive testers calls the given testing function on all values up to the given size and stops as soon as a counterexample is found.
random: The operation Quickcheck_Random.random of the type class random generates a pseudo-random value of the given size and a lazy term reconstruction of the value in the type Code_Evaluation.term. A pseudo-randomness generator is defined in theory HOL.Random.
narrowing: narrowing implements Haskell’s Lazy Smallcheck using the type classes narrowing and partial_term_of. Variables in the current goal are initially represented as symbolic variables. The execution of the goal tries to evaluate one of them, the test engine replaces it with refinements provided by narrowing. Narrowing views every value as a sum-of-products which is expressed using the operations Quickcheck_Narrowing.cons, Quickcheck_Narrowing.apply and Quickcheck_Narrowing.sum. To reconstruct counterexamples, partial_term_of transforms narrowing’s deep representation of terms to the type Code_Evaluation.term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose exhaustive for completeness up to a size, random for sampling coverage, narrowing for symbolic search when evaluation can guide refinements. Ensure appropriate type class instances (exhaustive/random/narrowing/partial_term_of) are provided for custom types.

rubrics_metrics.name: nitpick and nitpick_params
rubrics_metrics.description:
nitpick tests the current goal for counterexamples using a reduction to first-order relational logic. See the Nitpick manual for details.
nitpick_params changes nitpick configuration options persistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Nitpick when you want counterexamples via relational-model search; adjust nitpick_params for persistent setup (e.g., backend options). Consult Nitpick manual for advanced options.

rubrics_metrics.name: find_unused_assms
rubrics_metrics.description: find_unused_assms finds potentially superfluous assumptions in theorems using quickcheck. It takes the theory name to be checked for superfluous assumptions as optional argument. If not provided, it checks the current theory. Options to the internal quickcheck invocations can be changed with common configuration declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run to locate unnecessary assumptions in theorems; configure internal quickcheck options if needed for thoroughness.

rubrics_metrics.name: coercion / coercive subtyping
rubrics_metrics.description: Coercive subtyping allows the user to omit explicit type conversions, also called coercions. Type inference will add them as necessary when parsing a term. coercion f registers a new coercion function f :: σ1 ⇒ σ2 where σ1 and σ2 are type constructors without arguments. Coercions are composed by the inference algorithm if needed. coercion_delete f deletes a preceding declaration. coercion_map registers a new map function to lift coercions through type constructors. coercion_args can be used to disallow coercions to be inserted in certain positions in a term. coercion_enabled enables the coercion inference algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register coercions only when their composition forms a lattice for completeness. Use coercion_map to support lifting through type constructors; be careful overwriting existing maps. Use coercion_args policies (−,+,0) to control where coercions may be inserted (prevent breaking syntactic constructs). Enable coercion inference explicitly via coercion_enabled.

rubrics_metrics.name: arith method and attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: arith decides linear arithmetic problems (on types nat, int, real). Any current facts are inserted into the goal before running the procedure. arith declares facts that are supplied to the arithmetic provers implicitly. linarith_split attribute declares case split rules to be expanded before arith is invoked. Note that a simpler (but faster) arithmetic prover is already invoked by the Simplifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use arith for decisive linear arithmetic obligations; declare supporting lemmas with arith attribute. Use linarith_split to expand splits needed by arith.

rubrics_metrics.name: iprover (intuitionistic proof search)
rubrics_metrics.description: iprover performs intuitionistic proof search, depending on specifically declared rules from the context, or given as explicit arguments. Chained facts are inserted into the goal before commencing proof search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify rules as intro, elim, or dest; mark safe rules with “!” (may be applied aggressively) and ignore rules with “?” (excluded from proof search). You may provide explicit weight annotations; otherwise the number of rule premises is used as weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: meson and metis (model elimination / resolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: meson implements Loveland’s model elimination procedure. metis combines ordered resolution and ordered paramodulation to find first-order (or mildly higher-order) proofs. The first optional argument to metis specifies a type encoding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use meson for model-elimination style proof search; use metis for resolution/paramodulation based automated proofs. See Sledgehammer manual for type-encoding details when invoking metis from automated tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: algebra method (Gröbner bases)
rubrics_metrics.description: algebra performs algebraic reasoning via Gröbner bases. The method handles two main classes of problems: (1) Universal problems over multivariate polynomials in a (semi)-ring/field/idom; method is only complete for algebraically closed fields. (2) All-exists problems of a restricted form (universally quantified equations e_i = 0 implying existence of y variables solving linear combinations p_ij * y_j = 0). The proof method is preceded by a simplification step, which may be modified by using the form (algebra add: ths1 del: ths2). algebra (as attribute) manages the default collection of pre-simplification rules of the above proof method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply algebra when your obligations are polynomial equations/inequations matching the described fragments. For completeness considerations, be aware that full completeness holds only over algebraically closed fields. Adjust pre-simplification rules with algebra add/del or algebra attribute to tailor the simplifier for your domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: coherent method
rubrics_metrics.description: coherent solves problems of Coherent Logic, which covers applications in confluence theory, lattice theory and projective geometry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use coherent for obligations that fall into Coherent Logic fragments; consult example theories for patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: unstructured case analysis and induction tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: case_tac and induct_tac admit to reason about inductive types. Rules are selected according to the declarations by the cases and induct attributes. These unstructured tactics feature both goal addressing and dynamic instantiation. Note that named rule cases are not provided as would be by the proper cases and induct proof methods. Unlike the induct method, induct_tac does not handle structured rule statements, only the compact object-logic conclusion of the subgoal being addressed. ind_cases and inductive_cases provide an interface to the internal mk_cases operation. ind_cases is a proof method to apply the result immediately as elimination rules; inductive_cases provides case split theorems at the theory level for later use. The for argument of the ind_cases method allows to specify a list of variables that should be generalized before applying the resulting rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer structured Isar methods (cases/induct) where named case rules and structured statements are needed. Use induct_tac/case_tac in tactic-style scripts. Use ind_cases for immediate elimination in proofs and inductive_cases to produce theory-level case theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: split_format (attribute)
rubrics_metrics.description: split_format (complete) causes arguments in function applications to be represented canonically according to their tuple type structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use split_format to canonicalize representation of tuple-structured arguments; be aware it may invent 'funny' names for new local parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: export_code (code generation: overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: export_code generates code for a given list of constants in the specified target language(s). If no serialization instruction is given, only abstract code is generated internally. Constants may be specified literally, by name._ for all executable constants within a theory, or _ for all executable constants currently available. By default, exported identifiers are minimized per module; suppress with open before the list of constants. For each involved theory one corresponding name space module is generated by default; a module name may be specified after the module_name keyword to place all code in this module. Generated code is output as logical files within the theory context, as well as session exports retrievable via isabelle export or isabelle build -e. All files have a common directory prefix: the long theory name plus “code”. The actual file name is determined by target language together with an optional file_preﬁx (default “export”). For SML/OCaml/Scala the file prefix becomes a plain file with appropriate extension; for Haskell it becomes a directory with separate .hs files per module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select constants carefully (use '_' or name._ for convenience). Use open to avoid identifier minimization per module. Specify module_name and file_prefix to control generated module/filenames. Use isabelle export / isabelle build -e to retrieve exported files from sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: export_target serializers (Haskell/Scala)
rubrics_metrics.description: Serializers take an optional list of arguments in parentheses. For Haskell a module name prefix may be given using the "root:" argument; "string_classes" adds a "deriving (Read, Show)" clause to each appropriate datatype declaration. For Scala, "case_insensitive" avoids name clashes on case-insensitive file systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass these serializer-specific arguments to customize generated language artifacts (Haskell deriving clauses, Scala case-insensitive handling).

rubrics_metrics.name: code / code equation variants
rubrics_metrics.description: code declares code equations for code generation. Variant code equation declares a conventional equation as code equation. Variant code_nbe accepts also non-left-linear equations for normalization by evaluation only. Multiple code equation / code_nbe declarations referring to the same constant within the same theory are handled as one function declaration for that constant: the first code declaration within a theory disregards any previous function declaration and supersedes any equations from preceding theories. Each code equation is prepended to existing code equations declared in the same theory, with syntactically subsumed equations removed. Packages usually provide reasonable default code equations; an explicit declaration of a code equation supersedes any preceding default code equations. Variants code_abstype and code_abstract declare abstract datatype certificates or code equations on abstract datatype representations respectively. Vanilla code falls back to code equation or code abstract depending on the syntactic shape of the underlying equation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare code equations for functions you want executable; use code_nbe for equations intended only for normalization-by-evaluation. Be aware of ordering and precedence: first explicit declaration in a theory supersedes previous defaults. Use abstract variants for abstract datatype representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: code drop / code abort variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Variants code drop: and code abort: take a list of constants as arguments and drop all code equations declared for them. In the case of abort, these constants if needed are implemented by program abort (exception). Variants code drop and code abort derive the affected constants from the underlying theorems interpreted as code equations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use drop/abort to remove or force-abort code generation for problematic constants (e.g., non-executable definitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: code_datatype
rubrics_metrics.description: code_datatype specifies a constructor set for a logical type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare constructor sets to guide code generation and narrowing/partial_term_of reconstructions for datatypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: print_codesetup and print_codeproc
rubrics_metrics.description: print_codesetup gives an overview on selected code equations and code generator datatypes. print_codeproc prints the setup of the code generator preprocessor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these diagnostics to inspect what the code generator will do (which equations/datatype encodings and preprocessing steps are active).

rubrics_metrics.name: code_unfold, code_post, code_abbrev
rubrics_metrics.description: code_unfold declares (or with option "del" removes) theorems which during preprocessing are applied as rewrite rules to any code equation or evaluation input. code_post declares (or with option "del" removes) theorems which are applied as rewrite rules to any result of an evaluation. code_abbrev declares (or with option "del" removes) equations which are applied as rewrite rules to any result of an evaluation and symmetrically during preprocessing to any code equation or evaluation input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use code_unfold to rewrite inputs before code generation/evaluation, code_post to rewrite/equationally simplify results, and code_abbrev for bidirectional abbreviations; manage with 'del' to undo.

rubrics_metrics.name: code_thms and code_deps
rubrics_metrics.description: code_thms prints a list of theorems representing the corresponding program containing all given constants after preprocessing. code_deps visualizes dependencies of theorems representing the corresponding program containing all given constants after preprocessing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to inspect the preprocessed program (thm representation) and dependency graph prior to serialization or execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: code_reserved and code_printing
rubrics_metrics.description: code_reserved declares a list of names as reserved for a given target, preventing it to be shadowed by any generated code. code_printing associates a series of symbols (constants, type constructors, classes, class relations, instances, module names) with target-specific serializations; omitting a serialization deletes an existing serialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use code_reserved to avoid naming clashes with hand-written code; use code_printing to control how logical symbols map to target language names/constructs (remove serializations to revert).

rubrics_metrics.name: code_monad and code_identiﬁer
rubrics_metrics.description: code_monad provides an auxiliary mechanism to generate monadic code for Haskell. code_identifier associates a series of symbols (constants, type constructors, classes, class relations, instances, module names) with target-specific hints how these symbols shall be named. These hints gain precedence over names for symbols with no hints at all. Conflicting hints are subject to name disambiguation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use code_monad to support monadic translation patterns for Haskell. Populate code_identifier to control naming; ensure your hints preserve necessary name-prefix structure in compound statements like type classes or datatypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: code_reﬂect
rubrics_metrics.description: code_reflect without a "file_prefix" argument compiles code into the system runtime environment and modifies the code generator setup that future invocations of system runtime code generation referring to one of the "datatypes" or "functions" entities use these precompiled entities. With a "file_prefix" argument, the corresponding code is generated/exported to the specified file (as for export_code) without modifying the code generator setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use code_reflect to compile code into the runtime for faster interactive execution; use file_prefix to produce exported files without changing current generator state.

rubrics_metrics.name: code_pred
rubrics_metrics.description: code_pred creates code equations for a predicate given a set of introduction rules. Optional mode annotations determine which arguments are supposed to be input or output. If alternative introduction rules are declared, one must prove a corresponding elimination rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use code_pred to obtain executable versions of inductive predicates; provide modes to indicate input/output positions and ensure elimination rules when multiple introductions exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: code_timing, code_simp_trace, code_runtime_trace
rubrics_metrics.description: code_timing scrapes timing samples from different stages of the code generator. code_simp_trace traces the simplifier when it is used with code equations. code_runtime_trace traces ML code generated dynamically for execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable these tracing/timing facilities for performance diagnosis of code generation and generated code execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: printing and target_syntax customizations
rubrics_metrics.description: There are code_printing / printing_const / printing_type_constructor / printing_class / printing_class_relation / printing_class_instance / printing_module forms and associated symbol_* kinds (symbol_const, symbol_type_constructor, symbol_class, symbol_class_relation, symbol_class_instance, symbol_module) to map logical symbols and modules to target-specific serializations and target_syntax settings (infix/infixl/infixr, rich_syntax etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use printing_* declarations to precisely control syntax and rendering of symbols in generated code; adapt infix declarations and rich_syntax flags for idiomatic target-language output.

rubrics_metrics.name: exported identifier minimization and open
rubrics_metrics.description: By default, exported identifiers are minimized per module. This can be suppressed by prepending open before the list of constants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use open when you want full names preserved across modules (avoid automatic minimization which may produce shorter but less predictable identifiers).

rubrics_metrics.name: selection of constants for export
rubrics_metrics.description: Constants may be specified by giving them literally, referring to all executable constants within a certain theory by giving name._, or referring to all executable constants currently available by giving _.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use name._ and _ for bulk selection, but be aware of unintentional inclusion of non-executable items; prefer explicit lists for precise control.

rubrics_metrics.name: code generation file layout and retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated code is output as logical files within the theory context, as well as session exports that can be retrieved using isabelle export, or isabelle build with option -e and suitable export_files specifications in the session ROOT entry. All files have a common directory prefix: the long theory name plus 'code'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan session ROOT export_files entries and use isabelle build -e / isabelle export to retrieve code artifacts produced during builds; know the directory layout for locating generated files.

rubrics_metrics.name: code generator preprocessing model (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Code generation is split conceptually in three steps: selection of code theorems, translation into an abstract executable view and serialization to a specific target language. Preprocessing applies code_unfold rewrites, builds program representation (code_thms), and allows further code_post/code_abbrev rewrites on results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the pipeline to customize each stage: pick/declare code equations, tune preprocessing (code_unfold), inspect program theorems (code_thms/code_deps), and control post-processing (code_post/code_abbrev) before serialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: modedecl / modes / mode declarations for code_pred and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: code_pred creates code equations for a predicate given a set of introduction rules. Optional mode annotations determine which arguments are supposed to be input or output. The manual also exposes modedecl / modes / mode constructs appearing in code generator interfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate predicates with modes so the code generator knows which arguments are inputs/outputs in generated procedures; ensure mode declarations in context match intended use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isar quick reference: proof commands and derived forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix lists the main grammar of Isar proof scripts (theorem, proof, reﬁnement, apply method, proper_proof, statement forms), primitives (fix, assume, then, have, show, using, unfolding, proof ... qed), abbreviations (by, .., ., from, with) and derived elements (also, moreover, ultimately, consider/obtain patterns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this quick reference to structure Isar proofs correctly: prefer structured proofs with 'proof ... qed' and use derived abbreviations for concise scripts. Follow recommended primitives to manage facts, local blocks, and proof flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isar diagnostic commands for printing internal objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic commands include print type / typ τ, print term / term t, print proposition / prop φ, print fact / thm a, and print_statement a to print facts in long statement form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these printers to inspect types, terms, propositions and theorem objects while developing proofs and code-generation setups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isar proof methods overview (single-step / repeated / search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single steps: assumption, this, rule a, standard, contradiction, cases t, induct x. Repeated steps: intro a, intro_classes, intro_locales, unfold_locales, elim a, unfold a. Intuitionistic proof search: iprover. Classical Reasoner / other methods also available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select appropriate proof methods: use assumption/this for trivial steps, rule/intro/elim for rule application, cases/induct for structural reasoning, and iprover/meson/metis/algebra for automated search. Understand which methods insert facts and how they interact with declared rules/attributes.
